lines.text: Eight of thirty-one astronauts in NASA's study had abnormal jugular-vein flow in flight.
Near Mars, a clot can't wait: NASA lists delays of up to 40 minutes, and no evacuation.
In our twelve test cases, five scored low. VTE Watch still flagged three: a seventy-five percent flow drop, a missing scan, and an emergency symptom.
Scans and symptoms go in, checks run onboard, and the flight surgeon signs every decision.
